annotations.name: @Action
annotations.summary: A state transition: `public static S name(S state, args... [, Ctx])`, or returning a record `(S state, JulcList<Payout> payouts)` to pay funds out of the contract.

annotations.name: @Admits
annotations.summary: An `@Action` through which an instance admits an object moving in from another instance of the same contract (ADR-0012 D3). Its first argument after the state (and the params) is the object's id (`byte[]`). The validator requires that object to be spent in the same transaction with a move (`Into`) naming this instance; the method decides whether to admit it and may update the instance's state. `value` names the owned record it admits (`@Admits("Hero")`): only moves of that type can arrive through it, and it can only be a move of that type that it admits. It may be left out when only one owned type has moves.

annotations.name: @AuthorizedBy
annotations.summary: The method needs the approval of a credential (ADR-0009 D3), named by a `Credential` field of the state, the owned record, or the `Params` record (`"params.field"`). A key credential must sign; a script credential must run in the transaction for a withdrawal (the withdraw-zero pattern), approving it by its own rules.

annotations.name: @Batched
annotations.summary: The `Action` may also run as an intent (ADR-0004): a user locks a request in their own UTxO, and a batcher applies many requests to the instance in one transaction, so concurrent writers do not contend. In a batch, `ctx.caller()` is the intent's owner (who signed when creating it), `ctx.received()` the amount the intent carries, `ctx.balance()` the contract's balance at that point of the fold, and `validFrom`/`validTo` the batch transaction's bounds. The action needs a `Ctx` parameter and cannot use `@SignedBy`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@ValidAfter` or `@ValidBefore`: authorise with `ctx.caller()` and check time with `Clock`. The batcher chooses which intents to include and, by choosing the validity range, when they run. An intent runs against whatever state the batch finds: take a bound (a minimum out, a maximum price) as an argument and check it.

elements.name: only
elements.doc:
The {@link Action} may also run as an intent (ADR-0004): a user locks a request in their own UTxO, and a batcher applies many requests to the instance in one transaction, so concurrent writers do not contend.

In a batch, `ctx.caller()` is the intent's owner (who signed when creating it), `ctx.received()` the amount the intent carries, `ctx.balance()` the contract's balance at that point of the fold, and `validFrom`/`validTo` the batch transaction's bounds. The action needs a {@link Ctx} parameter and cannot use `@SignedBy`, `@OnlyOwner`, `@ValidAfter` or `@ValidBefore`: authorise with `ctx.caller()` and check time with {@link Clock}.

The batcher chooses which intents to include and, by choosing the validity range, when they run. An intent runs against whatever state the batch finds: take a bound (a minimum out, a maximum price) as an argument and check it. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.METHOD) public @interface Batched { /** Only as an intent: no direct call, so nobody can invalidate pending batches by spending the instance directly.

annotations.name: @Certify
annotations.summary: Decides which certificates of the contract's credential are allowed (ADR-0010 D1): `(Params cfg, TxCert cert)` returning `boolean`. Unregistration, committee and pool certificates are refused before it runs. Needs `@Quorum` or `@AuthorizedBy` over `params.*`.

annotations.name: @Destroy
annotations.summary: Ends the instance: `public static JulcList<Payout> name(S state, args... [, Ctx])`. The thread token is burned and the returned payouts must allocate the contract's whole balance.

annotations.name: @Init
annotations.summary: The constructor: `public static S init(args... [, Ctx])`. Exactly one per contract; its return type is the state type. Deploying an instance mints its thread token and checks the initial datum equals this method's result.

annotations.name: @Into
annotations.summary: Marks the destination of a move (ADR-0012 D3): an `@OwnedAction` parameter of the state type, after the `@Shared` source if any. The object moves to that instance, which is spent in the same transaction with an `Admits` action naming the object; the method gets the destination's state as it was before. The redeemer carries the destination's id, and both validators check each other's redeemer (I43).

annotations.name: @Invariant
annotations.summary: A rule every state must keep (ADR-0009 D4): a static method taking the state (or the owned record), optionally the `Params` record, and returning `boolean`. The validator checks it on every state it accepts as an output (creation and every action); the runtime checks it before submitting.

annotations.name: @Migrate
annotations.summary: A creation that adopts an instance of the previous contract version (ADR-0011 D4): `(Params cfg, Old.State old, args..., [Ctx])` returning the new state. `from` names a `byte[]` field of the params holding the previous policy. The seed is the old state UTxO, whose token must be burned in the same transaction; the new instance holds exactly the old lovelace and the new token.

annotations.name: @MigrateTo
annotations.summary: On a `Destroy`: the instance migrates to its successor contract (ADR-0011 D4). `value` names a `byte[]` field holding the successor's policy: a state field an admin sets, or `params.*`. The validator requires that the successor mints the instance id `blake2b_256(own input)`, and that its output holds at least everything this instance holds, less the payouts.

annotations.name: @OnlyOwner
annotations.summary: Shorthand for `@SignedBy("owner")`.

annotations.name: @Owned
annotations.summary: Marks the contract's owned record (ADR-0003): each owned object is its own UTxO, touched only by owned methods, so different objects never contend. A contract may declare several (ADR-0012 D1). Naming a `byte[]` component as `#key()` makes the type keyed (ADR-0016): at most one object per key and instance, kept in a sorted on-chain list. A keyed type is created by inserting next to its predecessor, needs an `@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)` exit, and every `@OwnedAction` on it must be authorized.

elements.name: key
elements.doc:
Marks the contract's owned record (ADR-0003): each owned object is its own UTxO, touched only by owned methods, so different objects never contend. A contract may declare several (ADR-0012 D1).

Naming a `byte[]` component as {@link #key()} makes the type keyed (ADR-0016): at most one object per key and instance, kept in a sorted on-chain list. A keyed type is created by inserting next to its predecessor, needs an `@OwnedDestroy(retire = true)` exit, and every `@OwnedAction` on it must be authorized. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.TYPE) public @interface Owned { /** The `byte[]` component that keys the object (ADR-0016 D1); empty (the default) for a plain owned type.

elements.name: maxKeyBytes
elements.doc: Longest key, in bytes: 1 to 64 (ADR-0016 D1).

elements.name: signedKey
elements.doc: The key is a 28-byte key hash that must sign the insert (ADR-0016 I53).

elements.name: linkCooldownMs
elements.doc: Least time between two relinks of a node, in POSIX ms (ADR-0016 D9): 0 (written explicitly; no churn protection) or 60,000 to 3,600,000.

elements.name: linkWindowMs
elements.doc: Widest validity window of a transaction that relinks a node, in POSIX ms (ADR-0016 D9): 20,000 to `min(900,000, maxValidityMs)`. `-1` (the default) means `min(120,000, maxValidityMs)`.

annotations.name: @OwnedAction
annotations.summary: Changes one owned object: `public static R name(R object, [@Shared S shared,] args... [, Ctx])`, or returns `(R value, JulcList<Payout> payouts)`. Spends only the object's UTxO.

annotations.name: @OwnedDestroy
annotations.summary: Ends an owned object: `public static JulcList<Payout> name(R object, [@Shared S shared,] args..., Ctx)`. Burns its token; the payouts must allocate everything it holds. On a keyed type (ADR-0016 D10), `retire = true` declares the retiring exit: the object stays as a retired node holding its deposit and its key (taken for good); the payouts allocate exactly `ctx.balance()`, everything but the deposit. A retiring exit needs nobody else, so it cannot take `@Shared`, `@Reads`, `@Payable`, `@Quorum`, `@AuthorizedBy`, `@ValidAfter` or `@ValidBefore`. Without `retire`, a keyed object's destroy removes it from the list and frees its key.

elements.name: retire
elements.doc:
Ends an owned object: `public static JulcList name(R object, [@Shared S shared,] args..., Ctx)`. Burns its token; the payouts must allocate everything it holds.

On a keyed type (ADR-0016 D10), `retire = true` declares the retiring exit: the object stays as a retired node holding its deposit and its key (taken for good); the payouts allocate exactly `ctx.balance()`, everything but the deposit. A retiring exit needs nobody else, so it cannot take `@Shared`, `@Reads`, `@Payable`, `@Quorum`, `@AuthorizedBy`, `@ValidAfter` or `@ValidBefore`. Without `retire`, a keyed object's destroy removes it from the list and frees its key. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.METHOD) public @interface OwnedDestroy { /** A keyed type's retiring exit (ADR-0016 D10).

annotations.name: @OwnedInit
annotations.summary: Creates an owned object: `public static R name([@Shared S shared,] args... [, Ctx])`. The object belongs to the instance it is created under.

annotations.name: @Params
annotations.summary: Marks the record of a contract's deploy-time parameters (ADR-0009 D1). They are applied to the script (JuLC partial application), so each parameter set has its own policy id and address. A method receives them by declaring a parameter of this type right after the state (or after `@Shared`; first in `@Init`).

annotations.name: @Payable
annotations.summary: The `Init` or `Action` may receive lovelace (`ctx.received() > 0`). Requires a `Ctx` parameter. Without it, `received` must be zero.

annotations.name: @Propose
annotations.summary: A constitution guardrail (ADR-0010 D1): `(Params cfg, ProposalProcedure p)` returning `boolean`. The ledger runs it for parameter-change and treasury-withdrawal proposals once a constitution names this script.

annotations.name: @Quorum
annotations.summary: M-of-N signatures (ADR-0009 D2): at least `threshold` (and at least one) of the transaction's signatories are among `keys`. Both name fields of the state (or the owned record): `keys` a `JulcList<byte[]>` of key hashes, `threshold` a `BigInteger`.

annotations.name: @Reads
annotations.summary: A method parameter that reads another JOUST contract's instance state through a reference input (ADR-0011 D2). `value` names a `ForeignInstance` field of the `Params` record (`"params.oracle"`); the parameter's type is that contract's state record. The validator checks the token kind, the single token, the script address and the inline datum's shape before decoding.

annotations.name: @Receives
annotations.summary: An action that takes deposits from other JOUST contracts in the same transaction (ADR-0011 D3). Its value equation adds every deposit claimed on its continuing output, and the method sees them in `funds.deposits()` (it must take `Funds`) to decide what to credit. An action without it takes no deposits: its exact value check fails if anyone adds value to its output.

annotations.name: @Shared
annotations.summary: Gives an owned method the instance's state, read-only, through a reference input: it is not spent, so it causes no contention (ADR-0003 D1). The parameter's type must be the state record.

annotations.name: @SignedBy
annotations.summary: The transaction must be signed by the key hash (`byte[]`) held in the named field of the current state.

elements.name: value
elements.doc: The transaction must be signed by the key hash (`byte[]`) held in the named field of the current state. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.METHOD) public @interface SignedBy { /** Name of a `byte[]` component of the state record.

annotations.name: @StateContract
annotations.summary: Marks a class as a JOUST state contract: a state record plus pure `Init`, `Action`, `Destroy` and `View` methods. The JOUST processor generates `<Name>Validator` (a JuLC `@MultiValidator`) and `<Name>Client` in the same package. JuLC treats `@StateContract` exactly like `@OnchainLibrary` (a fixed alias, bloxbean/julc#311), so it compiles the contract class for on-chain use without a second annotation.

elements.name: minAda
elements.doc:
Marks a class as a JOUST state contract: a state record plus pure {@link Init}, {@link Action}, {@link Destroy} and {@link View} methods. The JOUST processor generates `Validator` (a JuLC `@MultiValidator`) and `Client` in the same package.

JuLC treats `@StateContract` exactly like `@OnchainLibrary` (a fixed alias, bloxbean/julc#311), so it compiles the contract class for on-chain use without a second annotation. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.TYPE) public @interface StateContract { /** Lovelace locked in the state UTxO as its min-ADA deposit, on top of the contract's funds. `0` (the default) derives it from {@link #maxDatumBytes()}: `4310 * (160 + 200 + maxDatumBytes)`, rounded up to 0.1 ADA. An explicit value below that is a compile error.

elements.name: maxDatumBytes
elements.doc: Largest serialised state the validator accepts. A transition that would grow the datum past it is rejected, so no call can push the state UTxO beyond what {@link #minAda()} covers and brick the instance.

elements.name: maxValidityMs
elements.doc: Widest validity interval (`validTo - validFrom`, POSIX ms) a call that reads {@link Ctx} may use. Bounds how stale or how far ahead `ctx.validFrom()` / `ctx.validTo()` can be.

elements.name: assetSlots
elements.doc: Native assets a state or object UTxO is expected to hold at most, for the min-ADA deposit: each adds about 80 bytes (ADR-0007). `-1` (the default) means 4 for contracts that handle native assets and 0 otherwise.

elements.name: stakeSelf
elements.doc: Stake the state UTxOs to this script (ADR-0010 D2): base addresses whose rewards and certificates follow its {@link Withdraw} and {@link Certify} handlers (both required). Default: enterprise addresses, no rewards.

annotations.name: @ValidAfter
annotations.summary: The transaction's validity interval must start at or after the time (POSIX ms, `BigInteger`) held in the named field of the current state.

elements.name: value
elements.doc: The transaction's validity interval must start at or after the time (POSIX ms, `BigInteger`) held in the named field of the current state. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.METHOD) public @interface ValidAfter { /** Name of a `BigInteger` component of the state record.

annotations.name: @ValidBefore
annotations.summary: The transaction's validity interval must end at or before the time (POSIX ms, `BigInteger`) held in the named field of the current state.

elements.name: value
elements.doc: The transaction's validity interval must end at or before the time (POSIX ms, `BigInteger`) held in the named field of the current state. / @Retention(RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @Target(ElementType.METHOD) public @interface ValidBefore { /** Name of a `BigInteger` component of the state record.

annotations.name: @View
annotations.summary: A read-only query, `public static T name(S state, args...)`. Runs off-chain only.

annotations.name: @Votes
annotations.summary: Decides the contract's votes as a DRep or committee member (ADR-0010 D1): `(Params cfg, Voter voter, GovernanceActionId action, Vote vote)` returning `boolean`, called for every vote it casts. Needs `@Quorum` or `@AuthorizedBy` over `params.*`.

annotations.name: @Withdraw
annotations.summary: Handles withdrawals of the contract's staking rewards (ADR-0010 D1): `(Params cfg, BigInteger amount, args..., [Ctx])` returning `JulcList<Send>` totalling exactly `amount`, claimed in the output registry. Needs `@Quorum` or `@AuthorizedBy` over `params.*`.

examples.name: counter
examples.exercises: Actions without value; an anyone-can-call action without `Ctx`; `@OnlyOwner`; `@Destroy` returning the deposit

examples.name: vault
examples.exercises: `@Payable` init and deposit; `@OnlyOwner @ValidAfter` withdraw returning payouts (`Result`); close

examples.name: escrow
examples.exercises: `@Payable @Init` (buyer funds it); two `@Destroy`s; `Clock.after` lets anyone refund after the deadline

examples.name: dex
examples.exercises: Option G (ADR-0007). A constant-product AMM for one ADA/token pair: reserves are what the UTxO holds (`Funds.held`); LP tokens are minted and burned by the contract's own policy (`mint`, `ByAction`); swaps send tokens with `Send`. Every call names exactly what it `accepted`

examples.name: market
examples.exercises: Option G (ADR-0007). An NFT marketplace: each listing is an owned object holding its NFT; `buy` (a `@Payable` owned destroy) pays the seller and sends the NFT to the buyer and a royalty to a script address with an inline datum; `cancel` is the escape hatch

examples.name: treasury
examples.exercises: Option I (ADR-0009). A multisig treasury: deploy-time `@Params` (a guardian credential and a payout cap), a council deciding by `@Quorum`, a guardian *script* freezing it through a zero withdrawal (`@AuthorizedBy`, with a bound `Approvals` redeemer), an `@Invariant`, and authenticated `Paid`/`CouncilChanged`/`Frozen` events

examples.name: staking
examples.exercises: Option J (ADR-0010). A council-governed vault whose state UTxOs are staked to its own script (`stakeSelf`): `@Certify` allows only registration and exact delegation to the params' pool, `@Withdraw` sends rewards only to the payee (claimed in the output registry), `@Votes` votes as a script DRep by quorum, `@Propose` is a treasury-withdrawal guardrail

examples.name: oracle
examples.exercises: Option K (ADR-0011). A price `Oracle` and a `Shop` that reads it with `@Reads` (pinned in params, token kind, address and datum shape checked, freshness checked by the shop). The DevKit test composes a purchase and another oracle's post into one transaction with `Compose`

examples.name: upgrade
examples.exercises: Option K (ADR-0011). `CounterV1` names a successor (`setSuccessor`) and migrates with `@Destroy @MigrateTo("successor")`; `CounterV2` adopts it with `@Migrate(from = "params.previous")`, keeping its count and funds, in one composed transaction

examples.name: guild
examples.exercises: Option L (ADR-0012). `Guild` has two owned types, `Hero` and `Item`. Each owned method runs only on its own type's datum, and each type has its own invariants. A hero moves to another guild with `@Into`, which that guild admits with `@Admits` in the same transaction (`transferAdmitted`). `Armory` holds `Vault` objects, each with a MerkleMap inventory

examples.name: fees
examples.exercises: ADR-0011 D3. A `Stall` deposits a 5% fee from each sale into a `Pot` instance fixed in its params. `Pot.collect` takes the deposit in with `@Receives` in the same composed transaction. The output registry carries the deposit claim, and both validators check their side

examples.name: locker
examples.exercises: ADR-0014. MerkleMaps with native assets. `Locker` holds a native token for many users, with their balances in a MerkleMap. `Safes` has owned safes, each holding tokens and a MerkleMap written at creation

examples.name: registry
examples.exercises: ADR-0016. Keyed objects: one UTxO per key, unique per instance, in a sorted on-chain list. `Ballot` is one ballot per voter, ever (`signedKey`: the voter signs the insert; the only exit `retire`s it, so the key stays taken). `Entry` is a name registry: `claim` (`@Payable`) or `grant` a name, `upgrade`, `withdraw`, `recover` by the guardians' `@Quorum`, then `release` (frees the name) or `retire` it. DevKit tests cover duplicate keys, concurrent inserts, the Link cooldown, a hostile predecessor and composition; the Wasm engine replays its recorded transactions (`fixtures/m3/registry`). A keyed registry is permanent: no `@Destroy`, no migration

examples.name: wallet
examples.exercises: ADR-0013. Wallet-signed transactions. A counter and a bank are used from an address-only `WalletAccount`: `Compose.prepare()`, a CIP-30-style witness set, `PreparedTx.submit`. `js/page.mjs` (Node, CSL) plays the page: it verifies the prepared transaction, refuses malicious variants, signs and submits. Run `npm install` in `examples/wallet/js` first

examples.name: dapp
examples.exercises: ADR-0013, phases 2 and 3. A browser dApp on DevKit (`./gradlew :examples:dapp:run`, then http://localhost:8095). It uses typed JS clients generated from the Counter and Bank descriptions (`joust-gen`), the prepare service (`julc-state-server`), a page that verifies every transaction and shows what it checked before a CIP-30 wallet signs, and a "malicious service" switch. `DappDevnetTest` runs the flows in Node. See [its README](dapp/README.md)

examples.name: token
examples.exercises: Option B (ADR-0002). An account-model token whose balances live in a `MerkleMap` (an unbounded map in a 32-byte root). MPF proofs are checked by the shared map verifier (withdraw-zero). The script is read by reference

examples.name: bank
examples.exercises: Option C (ADR-0003). Shared bank config plus one owned account per customer. Customers act in parallel; withdrawals read the config by reference; closing works even if the bank is paused

examples.name: pool
examples.exercises: Option D (ADR-0004). `@Batched` donations and order-dependent ticket sales as intents: users lock requests concurrently, a permissionless batcher applies them in one transaction (refunds, change payouts, a cancel, an expired intent)

examples.name: dsl
examples.exercises: Option E (ADR-0005, ADR-0018). Contracts written in `.jsc` and lowered to Java at build time: `Jar.jsc` (tips, also as intents; a withdraw rule in an `if`), `Points.jsc` (a `BigMap<Key, Int>`, where 0 removes a holder, and self-transfer) and `Guards.jsc` (laziness of untaken arms and `\|\|`)

examples.name: rollup
examples.exercises: Option F spike (ADR-0006). An off-chain payments ledger (`Ledger`, a total JuLC-subset program with ed25519-signed orders) checkpointed by an L1 `Rollup` contract: commit the steps, a challenge window, finalize, and one-step fraud proofs that re-run `Ledger.step` on-chain and slash the bond

examples.name: crowdfund
examples.exercises: A `JulcMap` in the state, kept canonical with `SortedMaps`; refunds paying the caller; `@SignedBy("creator")`; capacity tested at `maxDatumBytes`

pages.title: Why JOUST
pages.description: The work a Cardano contract normally needs, what JOUST does instead, what it generates and checks for you, and where the project stands today.

pages.title: How JOUST works
pages.description: The architecture end to end - the annotation processor, the generated validator and client, the runtime, an instance's life as UTxOs, storage strategies and the npm path.

pages.title: Quick start: Java & Gradle
pages.description: Run the counter example, then set up your own Gradle project with JOUST, write a contract, test it and run it on Yaci DevKit.

pages.title: Your first contract
pages.description: Build the counter step by step - state, @Init, actions with and without Ctx, @OnlyOwner, @View, @Destroy - then run it on Yaci DevKit from Java or JavaScript.

pages.title: Quick start: JavaScript & TypeScript
pages.description: (Experimental) Create a JOUST app with npm only, build and deploy its Counter contract on Yaci DevKit, and call it from a Node script, a test and a browser page.

pages.title: Vault: deposits, time and payouts
pages.description: Build and run a time-locked savings vault on Yaci DevKit, with payable deposits, an owner-only withdraw after a deadline, payouts and close.

pages.title: Escrow and crowdfunding
pages.description: Two contracts with several parties - an escrow with two ways to end and a deadline refund, and a crowdfund with a canonical map of backers, refunds and a size cap.

pages.title: Token balances in a MerkleMap
pages.description: Run an account-model token whose balances live in a MerkleMap, from Java on DevKit and from a browser page that reads balances from its own mirror.

pages.title: Bank: owned objects
pages.description: Run a bank where each customer's account is its own UTxO, so customers act in parallel, with shared settings read by reference and an escape hatch.

pages.title: Pool: batched intents
pages.description: Run a community pool where donations and rising-price ticket sales arrive as intents and a permissionless batcher applies them in one transaction.

pages.title: DEX: native assets and LP tokens
pages.description: Run a constant-product AMM that holds a token reserve, mints and burns LP tokens and swaps with slippage bounds; then a look at an NFT marketplace.

pages.title: Multisig treasury
pages.description: A council-governed treasury with deploy-time @Params, @Quorum payments, a guardian script approving through a zero withdrawal, an @Invariant and authenticated events.

pages.title: Oracle and composition
pages.description: Run a price oracle and a shop that reads it with @Reads, then put calls to both contracts into one atomic transaction with Compose.

pages.title: Staked vault and governance
pages.description: Run a council-governed vault whose funds earn staking rewards; delegate by quorum with @Certify, collect rewards with @Withdraw, and vote as a script DRep.

pages.title: Upgrading a contract
pages.description: Migrate a live CounterV1 instance, with its count and funds, into CounterV2 in one composed transaction on Yaci DevKit.

pages.title: A counter dApp in the browser
pages.description: Build the template's Counter dApp end to end, from the Java contract to a page that prepares, checks and signs its own transactions.

pages.title: Deploy to preview
pages.description: Take the Counter dApp from Yaci DevKit to Cardano's preview testnet, run it with Eternl or Lace, and ship the page as static files.

pages.title: State and lifecycle
pages.description: The state record, @StateContract options, the @Init/@Action/@View/@Destroy method shapes, instance ids, datum size limits and maps kept canonical.

pages.title: Ctx, funds and payouts
pages.description: Read the caller, payments, balance and time through Ctx, accept lovelace with @Payable, pay it out with Payouts, and return everything on @Destroy.

pages.title: Authorization
pages.description: Decide who may call each method with Ctx.caller, @SignedBy and @OnlyOwner, M-of-N @Quorum, and @AuthorizedBy keys or withdraw-zero governor scripts.

pages.title: Time
pages.description: Deadlines and time locks on Cardano with validity intervals, Ctx.validFrom/validTo, Clock.after/before, @ValidAfter/@ValidBefore, TTLs and maxValidityMs.

pages.title: Require and errors
pages.description: Write contract rules with Require.that, see how a refusal reaches Java and JavaScript callers, and debug a transaction that fails on chain.

pages.title: Params, invariants and events
pages.description: Fix values at deploy time with @Params, enforce rules on every state with @Invariant, and emit events that indexers can trust.

pages.title: MerkleMaps
pages.description: Keep an unbounded map in a 32-byte root. How MerkleMap fields work, the MerkleMaps API, what the map verifier checks and the rules to follow.

pages.title: Owned objects
pages.description: Give each user their own UTxO with @Owned records, so calls never queue. Owned methods, @Shared reads, several types, moves and maps inside objects.

pages.title: Keyed objects
pages.description: At most one object per key, each in its own UTxO, kept in a sorted on-chain list. @Owned(key = ...), inserts, removes, retires, cooldowns, the Java client.

pages.title: Batched intents
pages.description: Let many users write one hot shared state without contention. @Batched actions run as intents that a permissionless batcher applies together.

pages.title: Native assets, mints and sends
pages.description: Hold native tokens in contract state, mint and burn your own tokens, and send outputs to any address with any datum, with every output counted once.

pages.title: Reads and composition
pages.description: Read another contract's state with @Reads, and put several contracts' calls in one atomic transaction with Compose, from Java and JavaScript.

pages.title: Deposits
pages.description: Pay value into another JOUST contract's instance in the same transaction, with @Receives on the receiving side and the output registry keeping both honest.

pages.title: Staking and governance
pages.description: Stake a contract's funds to its own script and govern rewards, certificates, DRep votes and proposals with @Withdraw, @Certify, @Votes and @Propose.

pages.title: Upgrades and migration
pages.description: Move a live instance, state and funds, to a new contract version with @MigrateTo on the old side and @Migrate on the new, in one composed transaction.

pages.title: Fees and script size
pages.description: What a JOUST call costs on Cardano (size fee, execution units, reference-script fee), measured script sizes and budgets, the 16 KB limit, and how to stay small.

pages.title: Security model
pages.description: What JOUST's generated validator enforces on chain, how the attack suite tests it, and what clients, pages, services and MerkleMap mirrors are trusted with.

pages.title: Testing
